metadata.title: README Checker: Does the README Actually Work?
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: Opens on my own intro, then the hesitant writer; terms card drawn in Manim; no verdict card or Your Turn (cut for the 2-4 minute limit). The locked ClaudeTitleOutro is replaced by an own drawn outro (B14) because it hard-codes @NikBearBrown, and the assignment forbids the instructor's credit line.
metadata.audience: hiring managers and engineers reviewing a Software Engineer candidate
metadata.source_doc: PROJECT-BRIEF.md; two manual README runs on 2026-10-13 (github.com/LavanyaRajesh24/webapp, github.com/heroku/node-js-getting-started)

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Luh-vun-ya. This is a pitch for my final project, the README Checker. Nothing is built yet.

shot.visual_intent: Title picture: the README Checker name, 'final project pitch · Lavanya', and 'nothing is built yet', beside a README page and an open box.
shot.motion_claim: Title picture: the README Checker name, 'final project pitch · Lavanya', and 'nothing is built yet', beside a README page and an open box.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: The question isn't how to fix a broken README. It's how to find out if it works.

show.event: types 'How do I fix a broken README'
corrects 'fix' to 'find' as the voice says it

props.text: How do I fix a broken README

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive question (fix) and corrects it to the real one (find).

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. A README: a project's setup instructions. A container: a throwaway sandbox where commands run without touching my laptop. And an agent loop: run a step, read the result, decide the next one.

shot.visual_intent: Terms card drawn in Manim: README, container, agent loop, one line each.
shot.motion_claim: Terms card drawn in Manim: README, container, agent loop, one line each.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: A new engineer opens a README and follows the setup steps. A step fails, and they can't tell if the problem is them, or the instructions.

shot.visual_intent: A README page with readable steps (clone, install, migrate, start); a cursor walks down and an X lands on migrate. Key line: 'Is it me, or the instructions?'
shot.motion_claim: A README page with readable steps (clone, install, migrate, start); a cursor walks down and an X lands on migrate. Key line: 'Is it me, or the instructions?'

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: On October thirteenth, I followed my own web app's README exactly as written, in a fresh copy. Here are its seven steps, and what happened at each one.

shot.visual_intent: My webapp README's seven real steps as readable rows; a mark lands beside each: placeholder warning, pass, fail, skipped, placeholder warning, fail, fail.
shot.motion_claim: My webapp README's seven real steps as readable rows; a mark lands beside each: placeholder warning, pass, fail, skipped, placeholder warning, fail, fail.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: The clone step had a placeholder instead of a real link. The database step failed on a missing config file. And the health check returned five oh three. I wrote that README, and it didn't work.

shot.visual_intent: A terminal panel with my real output from 2026-10-13: the migrate error and the 503 response.
shot.motion_claim: A terminal panel with my real output from 2026-10-13: the migrate error and the 503 response.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Then I tried Heroku's open source starter app, following its README the same way. It worked. The server started and the page loaded.

shot.visual_intent: The Heroku starter README's steps as readable rows; checks land on all of them.
shot.motion_claim: The Heroku starter README's steps as readable rows; checks land on all of them.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: But its README asked for the Heroku tool, which I didn't need, and never mentioned the npm version it wanted. So a good checker has to tell broken apart from mostly fine.

shot.visual_intent: A terminal panel with my real Heroku output: command not found, the npm engine warning, Listening on 5006, 200 OK.
shot.motion_claim: A terminal panel with my real Heroku output: command not found, the npm engine warning, Listening on 5006, 200 OK.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: So, the README Checker. A command line tool, in a public GitHub repo, that will run every README step inside a throwaway container.

shot.visual_intent: Open box (the container); the README drops in. Key line: 'Runs every README step in a throwaway container.'
shot.motion_claim: Open box (the container); the README drops in. Key line: 'Runs every README step in a throwaway container.'

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: It will run one step, read the real output, and decide what's next: continue, stop, or mark the step unclear. The AI picks the move, but every result comes from a command that actually ran.

shot.visual_intent: Run → read → decide loop beside the box; a dot travels the loop.
shot.motion_claim: Run → read → decide loop beside the box; a dot travels the loop.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Then it will write a report: pass, warning, or fail for each step, with the README line and the real error. This one is a mock up. It isn't built yet.

shot.visual_intent: A readable report mock-up for my webapp README with README line numbers, stamped 'constructed mock-up'.
shot.motion_claim: A readable report mock-up for my webapp README with README line numbers, stamped 'constructed mock-up'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Isn't that what CI does? My project's CI installs Node and the database with its own steps, separate from the README. CI tests the code, not the instructions a person reads.

shot.visual_intent: My real CI steps on one side, the README steps on the other; the CI run passes, the README is never touched.
shot.motion_claim: My real CI steps on one side, the README steps on the other; the CI run passes, the README is never touched.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: I'm aiming for software engineer roles. A hiring manager will run one command on a sample project, and within a minute, see a report they can check against the README.

shot.visual_intent: A terminal window with the planned command (constructed); a report appears. Key line: one command, one minute.
shot.motion_claim: A terminal window with the planned command (constructed); a report appears. Key line: one command, one minute.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: To prove it works, I'll build about ten sample projects, some with problems I plant, and some that work. I'll score how many problems it catches, and how many false alarms it raises. Those numbers don't exist yet.

shot.visual_intent: Ten sample boxes, planted bugs marked, a scan, and two empty score slots: caught ? / planted, false alarms ?.
shot.motion_claim: Ten sample boxes, planted bugs marked, a scan, and two empty score slots: caught ? / planted, false alarms ?.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: That will show five course skills: an agent loop, verification with real output, evaluation with a score, source grounding to README lines, and a prompt contract my code checks.

shot.visual_intent: Five labelled skills listed beside the box, each landing as it is named.
shot.motion_claim: Five labelled skills listed beside the box, each landing as it is named.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: It won't fix READMEs. It only reports. First, one sample README runs in a container and writes report dot md. If that file appears with a real exit code for every step, it ran.

shot.visual_intent: Out: a crossed-out pen ('won't fix'). First: README → box → report.md with exit codes.
shot.motion_claim: Out: a crossed-out pen ('won't fix'). First: README → box → report.md with exit codes.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: The risk: a README can contain any command. So every step will run in a disposable container, with no secrets, deleted after each run. Vague steps get marked unclear, not guessed.

shot.visual_intent: A locked box swapped for a fresh one; a vague step marked 'unclear'.
shot.motion_claim: A locked box swapped for a fresh one; a vague step marked 'unclear'.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? It's a mix. My public web app repo shows CI and cloud work: GitHub Actions, and AWS and GCP machine images. Docker I've used, but with no public proof yet. The agent loop, evaluation, grounding, and prompt contracts are new to me.

shot.visual_intent: Two labelled columns: skills I have (with the repo as proof), and skills that are new to me.
shot.motion_claim: Two labelled columns: skills I have (with the repo as proof), and skills that are new to me.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn picture per beat on a cream stage; the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived.
